newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Busang gold deposit set in Indonesia rainforests.
newsitem.headline: Busang gold deposit set in Indonesia rainforests.

text.p: Indonesia's huge Busang gold deposit is located beneath tropical rainforests on rolling hills in East Kalimantan province on Borneo Island.
"Busang is in difficult terrain. It's hilly, in dense jungle without any infrastructure and is thinly populated," said the head of a mining company that has a project in the region.
"It lacks proper roads and infrastructure, but has a fantastic river system that can take barges of up to 1,000 tonnes," he said.
The Busang property was discovered by Canada's Bre-X Minerals Ltd which estimates it contains at least 70.95 million ounces of gold currently worth over $24 billion.
Bre-X announced on Monday a partnership deal under which it is to take a 45-percent stake in a joint venture company to develop Busang.

It said in a statement: "The joint venture will be 45 percent owned by Bre-X, 30 percent by two Indonesian companies and their partners, 10 percent by the Republic of Indonesia and 15 percent by Freeport McMoRan Copper and Gold "
Freeport is to develop and operate the site.
"We are confident that, as the project drilling and mine construction are finalised, the proven gold reserves will grow substantially," Bre-X chief executive officer David Walsh said.
The deposit is some 200 km (125 miles) northeast of the East Kalimantan capital, Samarinda, and is traversed by a tributary of the Mahakam River.
It lies 250 km (150 miles) east of the border with Malaysia's Sarawak state which shares Borneo island with Malaysia's Sabah state, the oil-rich kingdom of Brunei and Indonesia's Kalimantan.
The Busang property is divided into three sections: Busang I or the central zone, Busang II in the southeast which contains the motherlode and Busang III to the north.
Industry sources said at least $1.75 billion would be needed to develop the property, with transport costs being cut by the presence of the Mahakam River's tributary in the region.
"The river is accessible to river traffic for up to seven months of the year," one industry source said. "It gets a little difficult during the dry season.
"The developer should be able to transport most of his equipment and ship out the ore through the river," he said. "The river system is good and can take fairly large barges."
Another industry source said a village was located some 50 km (30 miles) from the Busang property, with most of the villagers growing papaya and other cash crops.
"It is a relatively small village, and would be a good source for workers at the property," he said.
He said the land around the property was relatively low, with hills rising about 200 to 300 meters (650 to 980 ft) above sea level.
The property is in East Kalimantan's Kutai regency, which houses Kutai National Park near the coast and the Kersik Luwai Orchid Forest inland.
A mining analyst said given the nature of the terrain around the deposit, she expected the gold to be fairly close to the surface.
"I don't think it would require underground mining," she said. "This will have a significant effect on mining costs."
